name: assertSubset
title: Returns the value when it is a subset of a set

origin.description: Returns the value when it is a subset of a set. Otherwise it stops with the check message.
origin.usage: assertSubset(x, choices, empty.ok = TRUE, fmatch = FALSE, .var.name = vname(x), add = NULL)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Value under test. A Python int is an R integer and a Python float is an R double.

arguments.name: fmatch
arguments.text: Ignored. Matching uses Python's base match.

arguments.name: .var.name
arguments.text: Name used in the assertion message.

arguments.name: add
arguments.text: Collection that stores the message instead of stopping.

origin.details: Returns the value when it is a subset of a set. Otherwise it stops with the check message.
origin.value: The value when the check passes. Otherwise the check stops.

translation.description: Returns the value when it is a subset of a set. Otherwise it stops with the check message.
translation.usage: assertSubset(x, choices, empty_ok=True, fmatch=False, var_name=None, add=None)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Value under test. A Python int is an R integer and a Python float is an R double.

arguments.name: empty_ok
arguments.text: When false, an empty value fails the check.

arguments.name: fmatch
arguments.text: Ignored. Matching uses Python's base match.

arguments.name: var_name
arguments.text: Name used in the assertion message.

arguments.name: add
arguments.text: Collection that stores the message instead of stopping.

translation.details: Returns the value when it is a subset of a set. Otherwise it stops with the check message.
translation.value: The value when the check passes. Otherwise the check raises CheckError.
translation.example:
from checkmate import *
from checkmate.rtypes import NA

letters = list('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz')

print(assertSubset("a", letters))
